59:def _get_indexer_at_least_n_items(shape, n_desired, from_end):
60:    assert 0 < n_desired <= math.prod(shape)
61:    cum_items = np.cumprod(shape[::-1])
62:    n_steps = np.argmax(cum_items >= n_desired)
63:    stop = math.ceil(float(n_desired) / np.r_[1, cum_items][n_steps])
64:    indexer = (
65:        ((-1 if from_end else 0),) * (len(shape) - 1 - n_steps)
66:        + ((slice(-stop, None) if from_end else slice(stop)),)
67:        + (slice(None),) * n_steps
68:    )

211:def format_array_flat(array, max_width: int):
212:    """Return a formatted string for as many items in the flattened version of
213:    array that will fit within max_width characters.
214:    """
215:    # every item will take up at least two characters, but we always want to
216:    # print at least first and last items
217:    max_possibly_relevant = min(max(array.size, 1), max(math.ceil(max_width / 2.0), 2))
218:    relevant_front_items = format_items(
219:        first_n_items(array, (max_possibly_relevant + 1) // 2)
220:    )
221:    relevant_back_items = format_items(last_n_items(array, max_possibly_relevant // 2))
222:    # interleave relevant front and back items:
223:    #     [a, b, c] and [y, z] -> [a, z, b, y, c]
224:    relevant_items = sum(
225:        zip_longest(relevant_front_items, reversed(relevant_back_items)), ()
226:    )[:max_possibly_relevant]
227:
228:    cum_len = np.cumsum([len(s) + 1 for s in relevant_items]) - 1
229:    if (array.size > 2) and (
230:        (max_possibly_relevant < array.size) or array_any(cum_len > max_width)
231:    ):
232:        padding = " ... "
233:        max_len = max(int(np.argmax(cum_len + len(padding) - 1 > max_width)), 2)
234:        count = min(array.size, max_len)
235:    else:
236:        count = array.size
237:        padding = "" if (count <= 1) else " "
238:
239:    num_front = (count + 1) // 2
240:    num_back = count - num_front
241:    # note that num_back is 0 <--> array.size is 0 or 1
242:    #                         <--> relevant_back_items is []
243:    pprint_str = "".join(
244:        [
245:            " ".join(relevant_front_items[:num_front]),
246:            padding,
247:            " ".join(relevant_back_items[-num_back:]),
248:        ]
249:    )

251:    # As a final check, if it's still too long even with the limit in values,
252:    # replace the end with an ellipsis
253:    # NB: this will still returns a full 3-character ellipsis when max_width < 3
254:    if len(pprint_str) > max_width:
255:        pprint_str = pprint_str[: max(max_width - 3, 0)] + "..."
256:
257:    return pprint_str
